neighbours.label: a request that the listener pass something on to a third person, at ' my' after give or send and at ' I' after tell (give my thanks to, tell him I)
fire: When you see Ana, give my thanks to her brother.
Next time you call, tell Grandpa I miss him.
Could you send my apologies to the committee?
If you meet them, tell them I got home safe.
On your way out, give my spare key to the janitor.
At the meeting, please tell Omar I agree.
Before you leave, send my notes over to Priya.
While you're there, give my coat to the man at the desk.
quiet: When you see Ana, wear my blue scarf to dinner.
Next time you call, ask Grandpa how he feels.
Could you read my essay for the committee?
If you run into them, tell them the way to the station.
Last week the clerk refused to give my spare key to the janitor.
During the meeting, please tell Omar the time.
Before you leave, check my notes for Priya.
While you're there, hang my coat on the hook by the desk.

short: asking the listener to pass something on
notes: Third round. Two tests of 'passing on greetings' failed because ' my' fired in near misses such as 'Give my car keys to him'. Probes suggest passing on is the distinction and greetings are one case: ' my' after wash, fix or clean stayed under 0.03.
